question: Anti-sterility vitamin is:
subject: Nutrition

explanations.A: B1 (thiamine) prevents beri-beri.
explanations.B: B2 (riboflavin) prevents cheilosis.
explanations.C: Vitamin E (tocopherol) is the anti-sterility/antioxidant vitamin.
explanations.D: K is the clotting (anti-haemorrhagic) vitamin.

question: A nurse is attempting to identify a patient's concerns. Which communication technique is most appropriate?
subject: Fundamentals

explanations.A: Silence supports rather than identifies concerns.
explanations.B: Reflection is useful but narrow.
explanations.C: Paraphrasing checks understanding, not exploration.
explanations.D: Open-ended questions invite the patient to share concerns broadly.

question: The photolabile vitamin (destroyed by light) is:
subject: Nutrition

explanations.A: Thiamine is heat-labile, not light.
explanations.B: Riboflavin (B2) is destroyed by exposure to light, hence photolabile.
explanations.C: Niacin is the most stable B vitamin.
explanations.D: Cholecalciferol (D3) is actually formed BY light, not destroyed.

question: A patient with which condition will most likely have difficulty conveying needs verbally?
subject: Medical-Surgical

explanations.A: Receptive (Wernicke) aphasia impairs comprehension and meaningful verbal expression of needs.
explanations.B: Hearing impaired patients can still speak.
explanations.C: Delirium fluctuates; many can still verbalize basic needs.
explanations.D: Blind patients have intact speech.

question: Best technique for refuse (waste) disposal in a hospital is:
subject: Community Health

explanations.A: Open burning releases dioxins and is unsafe.
explanations.B: Dumping is unsafe for biomedical waste.
explanations.C: Composting is for biodegradable kitchen waste, not infectious.
explanations.D: Engineered incineration is the recommended hospital biomedical waste destruction method.

question: Recommended maximum permissible level of community noise is:
subject: Community Health

explanations.A: 50 dB is closer to a residential daytime guideline.
explanations.B: 60 dB is conversational level.
explanations.C: 35 dB is a hospital ward target.
explanations.D: 85 dB is the OSHA permissible occupational exposure limit before hearing protection is required.

question: International Women's Day is observed on:
subject: Community Health

explanations.A: World TB Day is March 24.
explanations.B: International Women's Day is observed on 8th March.
explanations.C: World Day Against Child Labour is June 12.
explanations.D: International Day of World's Indigenous Peoples is Aug 9.

question: Antitubercular drug contraindicated in pregnancy is:
subject: Pharmacology

explanations.A: Ethambutol is considered safe with monitoring.
explanations.B: INH is given with pyridoxine; safe.
explanations.C: Streptomycin is ototoxic to the fetus and contraindicated in pregnancy.
explanations.D: Rifampicin is broadly safe in standard regimens.

question: Isolation duration for a measles client is approximately:
subject: Community Health

explanations.A: 2 days is far too short.
explanations.B: Isolation is recommended for ~4-5 days from rash onset (infectious 4 days before to 4-5 days after).
explanations.C: 7 days is beyond infectious period.
explanations.D: 15 days is for pertussis-like long-isolation diseases.

question: Koplik's spots are characteristic of:
subject: Microbiology

explanations.A: Rubella has Forschheimer spots, not Koplik.
explanations.B: Typhoid shows rose spots on trunk.
explanations.C: Bluish-white Koplik spots on buccal mucosa are pathognomonic of measles.
explanations.D: Mumps causes parotid swelling, not oral spots.

question: Causative organism of chickenpox is:
subject: Microbiology

explanations.A: Variola caused smallpox (eradicated).
explanations.B: Varicella zoster virus (HHV-3) causes chickenpox and shingles.
explanations.C: Myxovirus (influenza) is unrelated.
explanations.D: Paramyxovirus causes measles/mumps.

question: Schick test is used in the diagnosis of:
subject: Microbiology

explanations.A: No skin test for measles.
explanations.B: Rubella is tested serologically.
explanations.C: No skin test for mumps.
explanations.D: Schick test detects susceptibility to diphtheria toxin (intradermal toxin).

question: Causative agent of swine flu is:
subject: Microbiology

explanations.A: H1N1 is the swine flu strain (2009 pandemic).
explanations.B: H2N2 caused the 1957 Asian flu pandemic.
explanations.C: H3N2 causes seasonal flu.
explanations.D: H5N1 is avian (bird) flu.

question: Smallpox was officially declared eradicated globally in:
subject: Community Health

explanations.A: Last natural case in Asia was 1975 but not declared eradicated yet.
explanations.B: Last natural case overall was 1977 in Somalia.
explanations.C: WHO formally declared smallpox eradicated on 8 May 1980.
explanations.D: Distractor year.

question: Most common cause of infant mortality in India is:
subject: Community Health

explanations.A: ARI is a major contributor but secondary.
explanations.B: CHD contributes a small share.
explanations.C: Low birth weight/prematurity is the leading underlying cause of infant deaths in India.
explanations.D: Diarrhoea is also a major contributor but secondary.

question: Maternal mortality rate is conventionally expressed per:
subject: OBG

explanations.A: Per 100 makes the rate trivially small.
explanations.B: IMR uses per 1000 live births, not MMR.
explanations.C: Not a standard denominator.
explanations.D: MMR is reported per 100,000 live births.

question: Dose of BCG vaccine for an infant under 1 year is:
subject: Community Health

explanations.A: For infants under 1 year, BCG dose is 0.05 mL intradermal at left deltoid.
explanations.B: 0.1 mL is the standard dose for those above 1 year.
explanations.C: BCG is never given subcutaneously.
explanations.D: BCG is never given intramuscularly.

question: ASHA worker primarily links the community with:
subject: Community Health

explanations.A: LHV supervises ANMs.
explanations.B: PHN works at PHC supervisory level.
explanations.C: ASHA is the village-level activist linking households to ANM and Anganwadi worker (and the health system).
explanations.D: District-level MO is too distant.

question: Disease transmissible from animals to humans is termed:
subject: Community Health

explanations.A: Zoonosis = disease transmissible from animals to humans (e.g., rabies, brucellosis).
explanations.B: Epizootic is an animal epidemic.
explanations.C: Enzootic is endemic in animals.
explanations.D: Anthroponosis is human-to-human transmission.

question: A patient on mannitol for raised ICP requires priority monitoring of:
subject: Medical-Surgical

explanations.A: AVP is rarely measured at bedside.
explanations.B: Urine SG changes but is not the dose-limiting parameter.
explanations.C: Creatinine is monitored but lags.
explanations.D: Serum osmolality (target <320 mOsm/kg) determines safe further dosing.

question: End-tidal CO2 reading of ~1 mmHg immediately after intubation most likely indicates:
subject: Medical-Surgical

explanations.A: PE drops EtCO2 but rarely to 1 mmHg.
explanations.B: Mainstem still produces a tracing.
explanations.C: Correct placement gives 35-45 mmHg.
explanations.D: A near-zero EtCO2 strongly suggests esophageal intubation; immediate re-intubation is required.

question: When administering massive transfusion with low fibrinogen (0.4 g/L), priority correction is:
subject: Medical-Surgical

explanations.A: Potassium bolus is dangerous and not indicated.
explanations.B: PCC corrects warfarin/factor deficiency, not fibrinogen.
explanations.C: Cryoprecipitate replenishes fibrinogen (target >1.5-2 g/L) in massive haemorrhage.
explanations.D: Protamine reverses heparin, irrelevant here.

question: Initial site for chickenpox rash is typically:
subject: Microbiology

explanations.A: Chickenpox rash is centripetal — starts on the trunk and spreads to face/limbs.
explanations.B: Face-first is more characteristic of smallpox (centrifugal).
explanations.C: Palms/soles distribution is uncommon.
explanations.D: Lower-limb-first is atypical.

question: Mumps primarily affects which gland?
subject: Microbiology

explanations.A: Submandibular involvement is uncommon and secondary.
explanations.B: Sublingual is rarely affected.
explanations.C: Parotid swelling is the hallmark of mumps.
explanations.D: Thyroid is unaffected.
